items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The boy who was with Tommy Dorsey. I know his name. Carmen Mastren.

ctx.x: I do that with the banjo, yeah. That’s what they wanted. Allan Reuss was a master. He was with Benny Goodman. That boy who was with Tommy Dorsey. I know his name. Carmen Mastren. We know one another. Allan Reuss. And there was what’s­ his-name, with Basie.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Tommy Dorsey used it in a lot of his records. ... Tommy Dorsey, all them bands was there. ... sell him some, and Tommy Dorsey and sell him some ... Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey, Bert Lom, Paul Whiteman, everybody, all the White musicians used to go to Pa and Jerry's

ctx.x: Yeah, that turnaround you hear. Tommy Dorsey used it in a lot of his records. Dig it, that's Willie Smith, the Lion. For a time, a lot of arrangers were using that quick...the quick turnaround. [SINGS REFRAIN] It will strike you. Your ears got to... Because you've got to know whether you're pressing all the right ones!...chords...

Well, the Lion's in there. My Uncle Paul had introduced me to Willie Smith, the Lion -- Paul Barbarin. He introduced me to him. He said, "This is the mighty Lion." There was the Lion on the corner; there was Jelly Roll looking at the Lion like he was a lamb. Jelly said, "Ah, he's a good piano player, but he's Classical. He ain't playing no Jazz." It was one of the things.
